bio:pellet-handling.label: Removing a supernatant without disturbing the pellet

bio:plate-absorbance-read.label: Reading absorbance on a plate reader

bio:subunit-structure.label: Subunit structure from native and denatured sizes

chem:liquid-liquid-extraction.label: Extracting and washing with a separating funnel

chem:rotary-evaporation.label: Drying an organic solution and taking off the solvent

chem:separation-design.label: Choosing a separation from the properties of the components

core:calibration-analysis.label: Building and using a calibration curve

core:experimental-design.label: Designing an experiment: question, hypothesis, treatments and replicates

core:hypothesis-testing.label: Choosing and applying a statistical test

core:inert-atmosphere.label: Working under an inert atmosphere: septa, balloons and syringes

core:pipette-range-selection.label: Choosing a pipette for the volume

core:sequence-analysis.label: Searching and aligning sequences, and reading what a mutation does

core:vacuum-filtration.label: Vacuum filtration and washing a filter cake

micro:aseptic-technique.label: Aseptic technique (flaming the loop, not contaminating cultures)

micro:top-agar-overlay.label: Pouring cells in molten top agar

activities.title: Accuracy and precision: a dye standard curve from a weighed stock
activities.summary: Weigh about 200 mg of a blue dye powder, make it up to 50.00 mL in a volumetric flask, dilute it to five standards, and measure their absorbance at 628 nm. Then read an unknown three times from fresh portions and report its concentration with the spread of the three.
terms: Accuracy and precision: a dye standard curve from a weighed stock

activities.title: The compound microscope: magnification, resolution and contrast
activities.summary: Set up a compound microscope, see which way round its image is, work up from 4× to 100× oil immersion on a stained blood smear, and compare bright field with phase contrast on living yeast. Then leave it clean.
terms: The compound microscope: magnification, resolution and contrast

activities.title: Checking micropipettes by weighing
activities.summary: Dispense 100 µL of water ten times from each of two P200 pipettes onto an analytical balance, convert each mass to a volume, and work out each pipette's systematic error (accuracy) and coefficient of variation (precision) against the limits for a 200 µL pipette.
terms: Accuracy and precision (systematic and random error)

activities.title: Micropipettes: choosing, using and proving them
activities.summary: Dispense three volumes of water with the pipette suited to each and check them on a balance. Pipette a viscous 50 % glycerol solution forward and in reverse and compare. Then pass a competency test: build exactly 1.000 mL of a four-part mixture in one tube and prove it by weight.
terms: Micropipettes: choosing, using and proving them

activities.title: Balance the rotor
activities.summary: A 30–60 second recall drill: load a microcentrifuge in balance. The number of tubes varies, so an odd number needs a balance tube.

activities.title: Protein concentration by BCA assay
activities.summary: Make a BSA standard series, assay it with two unknowns in a 96-well plate, and read the unknowns from the standard curve. One unknown is too concentrated and must be diluted and re-assayed.

activities.title: What kind of inhibitor is oxamate?
activities.summary: Measure lactate dehydrogenase's initial rates across a range of pyruvate concentrations with and without oxamate, fit Km and Vmax to each set, and decide from how they change what kind of inhibitor oxamate is.
terms: What kind of inhibitor is oxamate?

activities.title: Purifying a His-tagged protein on nickel
activities.summary: Load a cleared E. coli lysate containing His-tagged GFP onto a nickel column, collect the flow-through, wash with 20 mM imidazole and elute with 250 mM imidazole. Follow the GFP by its absorbance at 488 nm to work out the yield, and check the purity of each fraction by SDS-PAGE.
terms: Purifying a His-tagged protein on nickel

activities.title: Finding one protein in a mixture: a Western blot
activities.summary: Run a crude protein extract, purified LDH and BSA on an SDS gel, blot it onto nitrocellulose, block, probe with a mouse anti-LDH antibody and an HRP-labelled anti-mouse antibody, develop with TMB, and size the band the antibody finds against a prestained marker.
terms: Finding one protein in a mixture: a Western blot

activities.title: A purification table: how pure, how much?
activities.summary: Purify His-tagged GFP from a lysate on a nickel column, then measure each stage: total protein by a Bradford assay against BSA standards, GFP by its absorbance at 488 nm. Build a purification table of total protein, total GFP, specific GFP, yield and fold purification.
terms: Yield, specific activity and fold purification
A purification table: how pure, how much?

activities.title: Quantifying antigen by ELISA: a four-parameter logistic standard curve
activities.summary: Coat an ELISA plate with an eight-point, three-fold ovalbumin standard series (3 µg/mL down to 0.004 µg/mL and a blank) and two samples, one of them also diluted twenty-fold. Fit a four-parameter logistic to the standards and read the samples from it, diluting any that lie above the curve.
terms: Quantifying antigen by ELISA: a four-parameter logistic standard curve

activities.title: Which kind of inhibitor? A global fit of alkaline phosphatase rates
activities.summary: Measure alkaline phosphatase's initial rates on pNPP at seven substrate concentrations, with no L-phenylalanine and with 2 and 6 mM. Fit all 21 rates at once to each inhibition mechanism, keep the one the data support best, and report its constants.
terms: Which kind of inhibitor? A global fit of alkaline phosphatase rates
global fit of alkaline phosphatase rates

activities.title: Rates from a continuous assay: replicates and substrate concentration
activities.summary: Make a substrate solution from a stock and dilute it twice, start each reaction in the cuvette with alkaline phosphatase, follow the yellow product at 405 nm for four minutes, and take the initial rate from each trace. Four replicates at each of three concentrations give a mean and a spread, and show how the rate depends on the substrate.
terms: Initial rates from a continuous assay
Rates from a continuous assay: replicates and substrate concentration

activities.title: Did induction work? An expression time course by SDS-PAGE
activities.summary: Take samples of an E. coli expression culture before and 1 and 3 hours after IPTG, boil the cell pellets in SDS sample buffer with DTT, run them beside the purified protein on a 4-20 % gel, and judge from the bands whether His6-GFP was overexpressed.
terms: Did induction work? An expression time course by SDS-PAGE

activities.title: A body-odour enzyme: substrate preference and a time-dependent inhibitor
activities.summary: Follow a skin bacterium's C-S β-lyase with Ellman's reagent: Michaelis–Menten series on two S-substituted cysteines give each one's kcat/Km, and pre-incubating the enzyme with L-cycloserine shows activity lost with time.
terms: kcat/Km as a measure of substrate preference
A body-odour enzyme: substrate preference and a time-dependent inhibitor

activities.title: KM and Vmax from initial rates: a substrate series, two ways to fit
activities.summary: Find p-nitrophenol's extinction coefficient from a standard, make a two-fold series of p-nitrophenyl phosphate, measure alkaline phosphatase's initial rate at each concentration in duplicate, and work out its specific activity and its KM and Vmax, from a double-reciprocal plot and from a direct Michaelis–Menten fit.
terms: What linear transformations do to errors
KM and Vmax from initial rates: a substrate series, two ways to fit

activities.title: Michaelis–Menten kinetics of lactate dehydrogenase
activities.summary: Measure the initial rate of NADH oxidation by lactate dehydrogenase across a range of pyruvate concentrations, and fit the Michaelis–Menten equation to find Km and Vmax.

activities.title: An immunisation course by ELISA: end-point titres, and what blocking is for
activities.summary: Coat a plate with a recombinant antigen, block all but two columns, titrate a goat's pre-immune serum and its sera after a prime and two boosts three-fold down the plate, detect bound goat IgG with a peroxidase anti-goat conjugate and TMB, and compare end-point titres; the unblocked columns show why blocking matters.
terms: An immunisation course by ELISA: end-point titres, and what blocking is for

activities.title: Charge, salt and pH: when does a cation exchanger hold a protein?
activities.summary: Run a mixture of blue dextran, cytochrome c and DNP-glycine on three CM-Sephadex columns, in 1 M potassium acetate at pH 6, in 0.1 M at pH 6 with a step to 1 M, and in 50 mM carbonate at pH 11; from the colours of the fractions explain when the beads sieve by size and when they hold the protein by charge.
terms: A protein's charge against pH and its pI
Charge, salt and pH: when does a cation exchanger hold a protein?
when does a cation exchanger hold a protein

activities.title: How much antibody? ELISA against a known standard, read in the working range
activities.summary: Titrate a purified antibody standard of known concentration and two sera (supplied at 1:10) two-fold down an antigen-coated plate in duplicate, detect bound antibody with a peroxidase conjugate and TMB, average duplicates, find where the curves saturate, fit the standard and read each serum only from its points in the working range.
terms: How much antibody? ELISA against a known standard, read in the working range

activities.title: Is it a monomer? Native mass by size-exclusion chromatography
activities.summary: Calibrate an analytical gel-filtration column with two mixtures of standard proteins (elution volume against ln MW), run three purified proteins, read their native masses from the calibration and, from their subunit masses on SDS-PAGE, decide whether each is a monomer, dimer or tetramer.
terms: Is it a monomer? Native mass by size-exclusion chromatography

activities.title: Masses by electrospray: a protein, its trapped intermediate, and the ion mode
activities.summary: Read lysozyme's mass from its electrospray charge envelope, then that of lysozyme treated with a fluorosugar inhibitor, and from the difference say what is bound and how; compare positive and negative ion modes for the protein and for an oligonucleotide.
terms: Masses by electrospray: a protein, its trapped intermediate, and the ion mode

activities.title: A hydrophobic probe: ANS binding to serum albumin by fluorescence
activities.summary: Scan ANS's absorption spectrum and check its concentration, compare its emission free and bound to BSA (brighter and blue-shifted), work out its Stokes shift, and titrate BSA into fixed ANS to fit an apparent binding constant, checking that the inner filter effect is negligible.
terms: Fluorescence, quantum yield and the Stokes shift
A hydrophobic probe: ANS binding to serum albumin by fluorescence

activities.title: Binding constants and energetics from SPR, van't Hoff, ITC and EMSA data
activities.summary: From supplied data: dissociation constants and selectivity from SPR rate constants, ΔH, ΔS and ΔG from a van't Hoff plot, the sign, stoichiometry and enthalpy of binding from an ITC isotherm, and Kds of DNA-binding mutants from EMSA.
terms: Binding constants and energetics from SPR, van't Hoff, ITC and EMSA data

activities.title: Native molecular weight by sedimentation equilibrium
activities.summary: From sedimentation-equilibrium scans at three speeds, fit ln A against r²/2 for the buoyant molecular weight, convert it with the partial specific volume, check it holds at every speed, and compare it with SEC for the protein's oligomeric state.
terms: Native molecular weight by sedimentation equilibrium

activities.title: Reading immune responses from data: T helper subsets, costimulation and killing
activities.summary: Judge from supplied data which T helper response each traveller mounts, what two knockout mice lack, whether T-cell proliferation needs CD80/CD86 costimulation, why a CTL fails to kill by the intrinsic pathway, and which tissue shows germinal centres.
terms: Reading immune responses from data: T helper subsets, costimulation and killing

activities.title: Conformations and binding from smFRET and NMR shift mapping
activities.summary: From single-molecule FRET, the distance between two dyes in each of a molecule's states and the rate of leaving one state; from NMR chemical-shift titrations, which of three ligands binds tightest and where.
terms: Conformations and binding from smFRET and NMR shift mapping

activities.title: Protein concentration by Bradford assay
activities.summary: The Bradford microplate assay: the same standard series, plate layout and analysis as the BCA assay, with a dye-binding reagent read at 595 nm after a few minutes at room temperature.

activities.title: From enzyme to structure: timing a crystal soak, screening crystals and averaging particles
activities.summary: Measure how fast galactocerebrosidase (GALC) turns over its nitrophenyl substrate at its pH optimum and in the crystal's soaking condition, by a stopped assay at 410 nm, and use one turnover's time to choose crystal soaks that trap substrate or product. Then read a crystallisation screen, cryoprotect and collect a dataset, and plan a cryo-EM reconstruction: how many particles to average, and when refinement has stopped improving.
terms: Crystallisation screening and the phase diagram

activities.title: Finding an unknown binding partner: crosslinking, pull-down and a peptide mass fingerprint
activities.summary: Plan how to find the unknown partner of a 56 kDa cytosolic bait protein with an affinity tag and a maleimide crosslinker, then read the pull-down's SDS-PAGE against a bait-alone control and identify the partner's band from its tryptic peptide masses.

activities.title: Reading protein structures: lysozyme's bonds, maps, an NMR ensemble and cryo-EM conformers
activities.summary: From measurements made on a 1.8 Å structure of lysozyme bound to chitopentaose (a residue table, S–S distances, acid–base distances and contacts), find the disulphide bonds and salt bridges, give the S–S length as a mean and standard deviation, and name the interactions that hold the core and the sugar. Then reason about map contouring, missing residues, NMR ensembles and cryo-EM conformers.
terms: Resolution and what a map shows
X-ray, NMR and cryo-EM models compared

activities.title: Catalase: oxygen from hydrogen peroxide
activities.summary: Add different volumes of catalase solution to hydrogen peroxide, collect the oxygen in a gas syringe and relate the initial rate to the amount of enzyme.
terms: Heat unfolds an enzyme and destroys its active site

activities.title: Catalase: temperature and rate
activities.summary: Warm hydrogen peroxide and catalase to 30, 40, 50 and 60 °C (and use one pair at room temperature), mix the same volumes, collect the oxygen in a gas syringe and find how the initial rate changes with temperature, and why it falls when the enzyme denatures.
terms: Heat unfolds an enzyme and destroys its active site

activities.title: Food tests
activities.summary: Test glucose, table sugar, starch, egg white, vegetable oil and water for starch (iodine), reducing sugar (Benedict’s), non-reducing sugar (acid, then Benedict’s), protein (biuret) and lipid (Sudan III).
terms: Each class of biological molecule has a specific chemical test
Reducing sugars reduce copper(II) to copper(I) oxide in hot alkali

activities.title: How much glucose? A Benedict’s colour series
activities.summary: Heat glucose standards from 0 to 2 % with Benedict’s reagent to see the colours run from blue through green, yellow and orange to brick red, then estimate the glucose in an unknown by matching its colour.
terms: How much glucose? A Benedict’s colour series

activities.title: Vitamin C in fruit juice with DCPIP
activities.summary: Find how much vitamin C solution decolourises 10 mL of blue DCPIP: first a 1 mg/mL ascorbic acid standard, then orange juice and an unknown juice, and work out their vitamin C content.
terms: A reducing agent decolourises an oxidised dye mole for mole
An unknown is measured against a standard treated the same way
Vitamin C in fruit juice with DCPIP

activities.title: Amylase and temperature: timing starch digestion with iodine
activities.summary: Digest 1 % starch with amylase at temperatures from room temperature to 70 °C, take a drop into iodine every 30 seconds until it no longer turns blue-black, and find the optimum temperature from the times.
terms: Amylase and temperature: timing starch digestion with iodine

activities.title: Amylase and pH: timing starch digestion with iodine
activities.summary: Digest 1 % starch with amylase at 37 °C in buffers from pH 4 to pH 9, sampling into iodine every 30 seconds, and find the optimum pH.
terms: Amylase and pH: timing starch digestion with iodine

activities.title: Protease and milk: enzyme concentration and rate
activities.summary: Add 0, 0.5, 1 and 2 mL of trypsin (made up to 2 mL with water) to cloudy milk suspension at 35 °C and time how long each takes to clear as the casein is digested.
terms: A protease cuts proteins into soluble peptides
Protease and milk: enzyme concentration and rate

activities.title: Protease and milk: temperature and rate
activities.summary: Time how long 1 % trypsin takes to clear milk suspension from room temperature to 60 °C, and find the optimum.
terms: A protease cuts proteins into soluble peptides
Protease and milk: temperature and rate

activities.title: Osmosis in potato tissue
activities.summary: Weigh potato cylinders, leave them in sucrose solutions from 0 to 1.0 M for an hour, blot and reweigh them, and find from the percentage change in mass the concentration at which they neither gain nor lose water.

activities.title: The water potential of potato tissue
activities.summary: Find the sucrose concentration isotonic with potato cells from the percentage change in mass of cylinders in 0–1.0 M sucrose, and work out the cells’ water potential from it (Ψ = −iCRT).
terms: The water potential of potato tissue

activities.title: Concentrating a protein by ammonium sulfate precipitation
activities.summary: Bring a BSA solution to 70 % saturation with ammonium sulfate, pellet the precipitate in a balanced microcentrifuge, remove the supernatant, redissolve the pellet in a smaller volume of PBS and check the recovery at 280 nm.
terms: Concentrating a protein by ammonium sulfate precipitation

activities.title: Beetroot membranes and temperature
activities.summary: Stand rinsed beetroot pieces in water from room temperature to 80 °C for 20 minutes, and measure with a colorimeter how much red pigment has leaked out at each temperature.
terms: Heat and solvents disrupt membranes, so cell contents leak out

activities.title: Beetroot membranes and ethanol
activities.summary: Stand rinsed beetroot pieces in ethanol solutions from 0 to 60 % at room temperature for 20 minutes, and measure the pigment that leaks with a colorimeter.
terms: Heat and solvents disrupt membranes, so cell contents leak out

activities.title: Yeast fermentation: which sugars?
activities.summary: Mix yeast with glucose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, lactose or water at 35 °C and measure how fast each gives off carbon dioxide into a gas syringe.
terms: Yeast respires anaerobically, turning sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide

activities.title: Yeast fermentation and temperature
activities.summary: Measure how fast yeast ferments glucose from 25 to 55 °C by the carbon dioxide collected in a gas syringe, and find where its enzymes begin to denature.
terms: Yeast respires anaerobically, turning sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide

activities.title: Respiration in yeast with methylene blue
activities.summary: Time how long respiring yeast takes to decolourise methylene blue at different temperatures, with controls without glucose and with heat-killed yeast.
terms: A redox indicator shows the rate at which respiration releases hydrogen
Respiration in yeast with methylene blue

activities.title: Mitosis in a root tip: the mitotic index
activities.summary: Count the cells at each stage of the cell cycle in five fields of a stained root tip squash at ×400, and work out the mitotic index and the share of time spent in each stage.
terms: The share of cells in mitosis measures how fast a tissue is dividing
Mitosis in a root tip: the mitotic index

activities.title: Stomatal density on the two sides of a leaf
activities.summary: Count stomata in five fields of view at ×400 on impressions of a leaf’s lower and upper epidermis, and work out the number per mm² from the area of the field of view.
terms: Most stomata are on the lower surface, where less water is lost
Stomatal density on the two sides of a leaf

activities.title: Plant and animal cells: wet mounts and stains
activities.summary: Make wet mounts of onion epidermis (in water and in iodine) and of cheek cells (in methylene blue), look at them at ×100 and ×400, and compare plant and animal cells.
terms: Plant cells have a cell wall; both have a nucleus, cytoplasm and membrane
Plant and animal cells: wet mounts and stains

activities.title: Plasmolysis in red onion cells
activities.summary: Mount strips of red onion epidermis in water and sucrose solutions from 0.2 to 0.8 M, count the plasmolysed cells under the microscope, and find the concentration at which half are plasmolysed and the solute potential of the cell sap.

activities.title: Photosynthesis in pondweed: light intensity
activities.summary: Put pondweed in hydrogencarbonate solution at different distances from a lamp and measure the oxygen it gives off with a gas syringe; relate the rate to light intensity.
terms: The rate of photosynthesis is set by whichever factor is in shortest supply

activities.title: Photosynthesis in pondweed: carbon dioxide concentration
activities.summary: Measure the oxygen pondweed gives off 10 cm from a lamp in sodium hydrogencarbonate solutions from 0 to 0.1 M, the source of its carbon dioxide.
terms: The rate of photosynthesis is set by whichever factor is in shortest supply
Photosynthesis in pondweed: carbon dioxide concentration

activities.title: Photosynthesis in pondweed: temperature
activities.summary: Measure the oxygen pondweed gives off 10 cm from a lamp with the tube in water from 10 to 45 °C.
terms: The rate of photosynthesis is set by whichever factor is in shortest supply

activities.title: Photosynthesis in pondweed: the colour of light
activities.summary: Measure the oxygen pondweed gives off 10 cm from a lamp in white light and through red, blue and green filters.
terms: The rate of photosynthesis is set by whichever factor is in shortest supply
Photosynthesis in pondweed: the colour of light

activities.title: The Hill reaction: chloroplasts reduce DCPIP in light
activities.summary: Mix isolated chloroplasts with blue DCPIP and time how long the blue takes to go in light, with controls in the dark, with boiled chloroplasts and without chloroplasts.
terms: The Hill reaction: chloroplasts reduce DCPIP in light

activities.title: Separating leaf pigments by thin-layer chromatography
activities.summary: Extract the pigments from leaves with propanone, run them on a TLC plate in a hexane–propanone solvent, and identify carotene, xanthophyll, the chlorophylls and phaeophytin by their colours and Rf values.
terms: Leaves hold several pigments that absorb different wavelengths
Separating leaf pigments by thin-layer chromatography

activities.title: The pH optimum of alkaline phosphatase
activities.summary: Run alkaline phosphatase on p-nitrophenyl phosphate for 10 minutes in buffers from pH 7.5 to 11, stop each reaction with sodium hydroxide, read the yellow p-nitrophenolate at 405 nm and find the pH at which the enzyme works fastest.
terms: Enzyme activity depends on ionisable groups, so on pH
The pH optimum of alkaline phosphatase

activities.title: Transpiration with a potometer: light intensity
activities.summary: Measure the water a leafy shoot takes up in a potometer in the dark and at different distances from a lamp, and relate it to the opening of the stomata.
terms: Transpiration with a potometer: light intensity

activities.title: Transpiration with a potometer: air movement
activities.summary: Measure the water a leafy shoot takes up 20 cm from a lamp in still air and with a fan on low and high.
terms: Transpiration with a potometer: air movement

activities.title: Transpiration with a potometer: humidity
activities.summary: Measure the water a leafy shoot takes up 20 cm from a lamp in open air, inside a bag with damp paper, and inside a bag with silica gel.

activities.title: Transpiration with a potometer: temperature
activities.summary: Measure the water a leafy shoot takes up in a lit growth cabinet at 10, 20 and 30 °C, the air at the same relative humidity.

activities.title: Primary productivity: the light and dark bottle method
activities.summary: Fill three BOD bottles with pond water, measure the oxygen in one at once, keep one in light and one in the dark for a day, and work out the respiration, net and gross primary productivity from their dissolved oxygen.
terms: Primary productivity: the light and dark bottle method

activities.title: Respirometer: oxygen uptake by germinating seeds
activities.summary: Measure the oxygen taken up by germinating peas in a respirometer over soda lime, with boiled peas, a thermobarometer of glass beads, and peas without soda lime as controls.
terms: Respirometer: oxygen uptake by germinating seeds

activities.title: Respirometer: seeds and small animals
activities.summary: Compare the oxygen uptake per gram of germinating peas, woodlice and maggots in respirometers over soda lime, with a thermobarometer.

activities.title: Respirometer: the effect of temperature on respiration
activities.summary: Measure the oxygen uptake of germinating peas over soda lime at 25, 30, 35 and 40 °C and find the temperature coefficient Q10.
terms: Respirometer: the effect of temperature on respiration

activities.title: Heat given out by germinating seeds
activities.summary: Fill one vacuum flask with germinating peas and another with boiled peas, plug them with cotton wool, and read their temperatures each day for three days.
terms: Respiration releases energy, some of it as heat
Heat given out by germinating seeds

activities.title: Fruit fly crosses: a monohybrid cross and the chi-squared test
activities.summary: Cross vestigial-winged females with wild-type males, score the F1, cross F1 flies together, score the F2, and test the 3 : 1 ratio with chi-squared.
terms: Fruit fly crosses: a monohybrid cross and the chi-squared test

activities.title: Fruit fly crosses: a dihybrid cross
activities.summary: Cross vestigial-winged, ebony-bodied females with wild-type males, interbreed the F1, and test the F2 against 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
terms: Fruit fly crosses: a dihybrid cross

activities.title: Fruit fly crosses: a sex-linked gene
activities.summary: Cross white-eyed females with red-eyed (wild-type) males and score the F1 and F2 by sex: white eyes follow the X chromosome.
terms: Fruit fly crosses: a sex-linked gene

activities.title: Linked genes: a test cross and the recombination frequency
activities.summary: Cross black-bodied, vestigial-winged females with wild-type males; test-cross the F1 females to black vestigial males; from the recombinants, find the recombination frequency and map distance between the two genes.
terms: Linked genes: a test cross and the recombination frequency

activities.title: Allele frequencies over generations: the Hardy–Weinberg principle
activities.summary: Start a population with equal numbers of vestigial and wild-type alleles, let it breed for four generations, and estimate the frequency of the vestigial allele each generation from the proportion of vestigial flies.
terms: Allele frequencies over generations: the Hardy–Weinberg principle

activities.title: Choice chamber: woodlice and humidity
activities.summary: Put 20 woodlice in a choice chamber with dry air on one side and humid air on the other, count them on each side every two minutes for ten minutes, and test the final counts against an even split.

activities.title: Choice chamber: woodlice and light
activities.summary: Put 20 woodlice in a choice chamber with one side under black card and the other in the light, both humid, and test whether they prefer the dark.

activities.title: Choice chamber: maggots and light
activities.summary: Put 20 blowfly maggots in a choice chamber, one side covered, and test their response to light.

activities.title: Choice chamber: fruit flies and light
activities.summary: Put 20 fruit flies in a choice chamber, one side covered, and test whether they move towards the light.
terms: Choice chamber: fruit flies and light

activities.title: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of temperature
activities.summary: Keep water fleas in pond water at room temperature and at 25, 30 and 35 °C, count each one’s heartbeats under the microscope for 15 seconds, and relate the rate to temperature.
terms: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of temperature

activities.title: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of caffeine
activities.summary: Count the heartbeats of water fleas in pond water and in 1, 2 and 5 mM caffeine at room temperature.
terms: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of caffeine

activities.title: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of ethanol
activities.summary: Count the heartbeats of water fleas in pond water and in 1, 2 and 5 % ethanol at room temperature.
terms: Daphnia heart rate: the effect of ethanol

activities.title: Subunit masses by SDS-PAGE
activities.summary: Denature BSA, lactate dehydrogenase, lysozyme and an unknown protein in SDS sample buffer, run them beside a protein marker on a 12 % SDS-polyacrylamide gel, estimate each chain's mass from the marker, and work out how many subunits LDH has.
terms: Separation of denatured proteins by chain mass

activities.title: The temperature optimum of alkaline phosphatase
activities.summary: Run alkaline phosphatase on pNPP at pH 10 for 10 minutes at temperatures from 25 to 65 °C, stop with sodium hydroxide, read the p-nitrophenolate at 405 nm and find the temperature at which the most product is made. Then test whether heat damage is undone by cooling.
terms: Rate and denaturation make an apparent optimum
The temperature optimum of alkaline phosphatase

activities.title: A protein's native mass by gel filtration
activities.summary: Calibrate a size-exclusion column with BSA, ovalbumin and cytochrome c, collecting 1 mL fractions and reading each at 280 nm. Then run lactate dehydrogenase, find its native molecular mass from the calibration, and combine it with its subunit mass from SDS-PAGE.
terms: Separation by size in a porous gel
A protein's native mass by gel filtration

activities.title: Measuring an antigen by indirect ELISA
activities.summary: Coat a high-binding plate with ovalbumin standards (0 to 3 µg/mL) and an unknown, block with BSA, detect with a mouse anti-ovalbumin antibody and an HRP-labelled anti-mouse antibody, develop with TMB, stop with acid, read at 450 nm and find the unknown's concentration from the standard curve.
terms: Antibody detection on a solid phase
Blocking and washing control the background
Measuring an antigen by indirect ELISA

activities.title: Standardising sodium hydroxide with potassium hydrogen phthalate
activities.summary: Weigh the primary standard KHP by difference, titrate it with the sodium hydroxide solution to a phenolphthalein end point (one rough, three accurate titrations), and calculate the hydroxide concentration.
terms: Standardising sodium hydroxide with potassium hydrogen phthalate

activities.title: Water hardness by EDTA titration
activities.summary: Titrate 50.00 mL portions of a hard water sample, buffered at pH 10 with Eriochrome Black T, with 0.0100 M EDTA until the wine red turns blue. Find the total hardness (calcium and magnesium) in mg/L as CaCO₃.

activities.title: An equilibrium constant by colorimetry: iron(III) thiocyanate
activities.summary: Calibrate the absorbance of FeSCN²⁺ at 447 nm with standards in a large excess of Fe³⁺, then measure five mixtures of 1.00 mM Fe³⁺ with 0.2–1.0 mM SCN⁻ and calculate Kc = [FeSCN²⁺] / ([Fe³⁺][SCN⁻]) for each.
terms: An equilibrium constant by colorimetry: iron(III) thiocyanate

activities.title: Iron(II) by permanganate: a redox titration, by eye and by electrode
activities.summary: Titrate 25.00 mL portions of an acidified iron(II) solution with 0.0200 M potassium permanganate to the first permanent pink, then follow a further portion with a platinum electrode, 1 mL at a time. Find the iron(II) concentration both ways, and the formal potential of Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ from the curve.
terms: Electrode potentials and the Nernst equation
Iron(II) by permanganate: a redox titration, by eye and by electrode
Platinum redox electrode with Ag/AgCl reference

activities.title: Vitamin C in fruit juice by iodine titration
activities.summary: Titrate 25.00 mL portions of fruit juice, with starch indicator, with 0.00500 M iodine until a blue-black colour lasts. Calculate the vitamin C content in mg per 100 mL.
terms: Vitamin C in fruit juice by iodine titration

activities.title: Nutrients in a stream: phosphate and nitrate by colorimetry
activities.summary: Calibrate the molybdenum-blue phosphate assay (840 nm) and the zinc-reduction Griess nitrate assay (548 nm), measure water from above and below a treatment works' effluent and the effluent itself, and keep every reading within its calibration.
terms: Turning an analyte into something that absorbs
Nutrients in a stream: phosphate and nitrate by colorimetry

activities.title: Substituent effects on ester hydrolysis: a Hammett plot from pseudo-first-order kinetics
activities.summary: Follow the hydrolysis of four 4-nitrophenyl benzoates (X = H, 4-Me, 4-Cl, 3-CF3) by the yellow 4-nitrophenolate they release at 405 nm, fit each trace for kobs, get the second-order rate constant from kobs against [OH⁻], and from a Hammett plot find ρ and what it says about the mechanism.
terms: Hydroxide attack on an ester carbonyl

activities.title: Fischer esterification and work-up: what does each wash do?
activities.summary: Esterify 4-nitrocinnamic acid in refluxing ethanol with sulfuric acid in two flasks side by side; quench, extract into ethyl acetate, wash only A with bicarbonate and both with brine, dry over magnesium sulfate, filter, take off the solvent, weigh, and compare the two crude esters' melting points.
terms: Fischer esterification and work-up: what does each wash do?

activities.title: Working under nitrogen: what each step keeps out
activities.summary: Bubble nitrogen through water in a septum-sealed flask, then move 10 mL of it four ways: a flushed syringe into a purged flask, an unflushed syringe into a purged flask, a flushed syringe into a flask of air, and pouring into a beaker. An hour later, read each one's dissolved oxygen.
terms: Inert atmospheres: septa, balloons and syringes
Working under nitrogen: what each step keeps out

activities.title: Acylating a phenol under nitrogen: following the work-up by IR
activities.summary: Make 4-nitrophenyl 4-chlorobenzoate from 4-nitrophenol and an excess of 4-chlorobenzoyl chloride with triethylamine in dried THF under nitrogen, then work it up, taking an IR spectrum of the organic layer before the bicarbonate washes and another of the product.
terms: Acylation of phenols by acid chlorides
Acylating a phenol under nitrogen: following the work-up by IR

activities.title: Titrating a strong acid with a strong base
activities.summary: Find the concentration of hydrochloric acid by titration with standard sodium hydroxide, using phenolphthalein.
terms: Titrating a strong acid with a strong base

activities.title: Titrating a weak acid with a strong base
activities.summary: Find the concentration of ethanoic acid by titration with standard sodium hydroxide, and see why phenolphthalein, not methyl orange, is the indicator.
terms: Titrating a weak acid with a strong base

activities.title: Titrating a weak base with a strong acid
activities.summary: Find the concentration of aqueous ammonia by titration with standard hydrochloric acid, using methyl orange.
terms: Titrating a weak base with a strong acid

activities.title: How much ethanoic acid is in vinegar?
activities.summary: Dilute vinegar tenfold in a volumetric flask, titrate it with standard sodium hydroxide, and work out the ethanoic acid concentration of the vinegar itself.
terms: How much ethanoic acid is in vinegar?

activities.title: Titrating sodium carbonate with hydrochloric acid
activities.summary: Find the concentration of a sodium carbonate solution by titration with standard hydrochloric acid to the methyl orange end point, where both protons have been taken up.
terms: Titrating sodium carbonate with hydrochloric acid

activities.title: Titrating sulfuric acid with sodium hydroxide
activities.summary: Find the concentration of dilute sulfuric acid by titration with standard sodium hydroxide; each sulfuric acid gives two protons.
terms: Titrating sulfuric acid with sodium hydroxide

activities.title: Chloride by the Mohr titration
activities.summary: Find the chloride concentration of a solution by titration with standard silver nitrate, using potassium chromate: the first permanent reddish tinge of silver chromate in the white silver chloride marks the end point.

activities.title: Purifying benzoic acid by recrystallisation from water
activities.summary: Recrystallise benzoic acid from a mixture with sodium chloride: dissolve it in near-boiling water, cool, collect the crystals by vacuum filtration, wash them with ice-cold water, dry, weigh and take a melting point.
terms: Purifying benzoic acid by recrystallisation from water

activities.title: Which metal ion? Hydroxide precipitates
activities.summary: Add sodium hydroxide to five solutions, a few drops and then in excess, and name each metal ion from the colour of its hydroxide and whether it dissolves again.

activities.title: Which metal ion? Ammonia and its complexes
activities.summary: Add ammonia solution to four solutions, a few drops and then in excess: some hydroxides dissolve again as ammine complexes, one of them deep blue.
terms: Which metal ion? Ammonia and its complexes

activities.title: Which halide? Silver nitrate and ammonia
activities.summary: Acidify three solutions, add silver nitrate, then dilute and concentrated ammonia, and name each halide from its precipitate and how readily ammonia dissolves it.
terms: Which halide? Silver nitrate and ammonia

activities.title: Is there sulfate? Barium chloride
activities.summary: Acidify three solutions with hydrochloric acid and add barium chloride: a white precipitate of barium sulfate shows sulfate.

activities.title: Magnesium and acid: following a reaction by gas volume
activities.summary: Drop magnesium ribbon into hydrochloric acid, collect the hydrogen in a gas syringe, read the volume every 10 seconds and explain the shape of the graph.
terms: Rate as the gradient of an amount–time graph
Magnesium and acid: following a reaction by gas volume

activities.title: Concentration and rate: magnesium in acid
activities.summary: Repeat the magnesium and acid reaction with the acid diluted to four concentrations, find each initial rate from the gas syringe and see how rate depends on concentration.
terms: Rate as the gradient of an amount–time graph
Concentration and rate: magnesium in acid

activities.title: Temperature and rate: an Arrhenius plot
activities.summary: Warm the acid to four temperatures in a water bath, measure the initial rate of hydrogen production at each, and find the activation energy from a plot of ln(rate) against 1/T.
terms: Rate as the gradient of an amount–time graph
Temperature and rate: an Arrhenius plot

activities.title: The molar volume of a gas
activities.summary: React weighed pieces of magnesium ribbon with excess acid, collect the hydrogen in a gas syringe and find the volume one mole of gas occupies from the gradient of volume against moles.
terms: Rate as the gradient of an amount–time graph
The molar volume of a gas

activities.title: Catalysts and rate: hydrogen peroxide and manganese(IV) oxide
activities.summary: Add different masses of manganese(IV) oxide to hydrogen peroxide, collect the oxygen in a gas syringe and see how the amount of catalyst changes the rate (and that without it almost nothing happens).
terms: Rate as the gradient of an amount–time graph
Catalysts and rate: hydrogen peroxide and manganese(IV) oxide

activities.title: Surface area and rate: marble chips and acid
activities.summary: React the same mass of marble as large, medium and small chips and as powder with hydrochloric acid on a balance, follow the mass lost as carbon dioxide escapes, and explain why smaller pieces react faster.
terms: Surface area to volume ratio and collision frequency
Surface area and rate: marble chips and acid

activities.title: Tests for gases: hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and ammonia
activities.summary: Make four gases in boiling tubes, test each with a lighted splint, a glowing splint, damp litmus paper and limewater, and name each gas from what you see.
terms: Tests for gases: hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and ammonia

activities.title: Calorimetry: the enthalpy of displacement
activities.summary: Add zinc powder to copper(II) sulfate in a polystyrene cup, follow the temperature, correct for heat loss by extrapolating the cooling line, and calculate the enthalpy change of the reaction.
terms: q = m c ΔT and the enthalpy change per mole
Correcting for heat loss by extrapolation

activities.title: Enthalpy of solution: salts dissolving
activities.summary: Dissolve ammonium nitrate, potassium chloride and calcium chloride in water in a calorimeter, measure each temperature change and calculate the enthalpy of solution per mole.
terms: q = m c ΔT and the enthalpy change per mole
Correcting for heat loss by extrapolation

activities.title: Hess's law: the hydration of copper(II) sulfate
activities.summary: Measure the enthalpy of solution of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate and of its pentahydrate, and use Hess's law to find the enthalpy change when the anhydrous salt takes up water.
terms: q = m c ΔT and the enthalpy change per mole
Correcting for heat loss by extrapolation
Hess's law: the hydration of copper(II) sulfate

activities.title: Exothermic and endothermic changes
activities.summary: Follow the temperature of four changes in a polystyrene cup (neutralisation, ammonium nitrate dissolving, citric acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate, magnesium in acid) and decide which give out heat and which take it in.
terms: q = m c ΔT and the enthalpy change per mole
Correcting for heat loss by extrapolation

activities.title: The reactivity series by displacement
activities.summary: Put magnesium, zinc, iron and copper into each other's sulfate solutions, look for deposits and colour changes, feel for warming, and work out the reactivity series.
terms: The reactivity series and electron transfer

activities.title: Metals with acid: comparing reactivity
activities.summary: Add magnesium, zinc, iron and copper to dilute hydrochloric acid, compare how hard each fizzes and how much it warms the acid, and place them in a reactivity series.
terms: The reactivity series and electron transfer

activities.title: Making copper(II) sulfate crystals from copper(II) oxide
activities.summary: Warm sulfuric acid, add copper(II) oxide until some is left over, filter off the excess, evaporate the blue filtrate and let it cool so that copper(II) sulfate crystals grow; dry and weigh them for a percentage yield.
terms: Making a soluble salt from an insoluble base
Making copper(II) sulfate crystals from copper(II) oxide

activities.title: Preparing an insoluble salt: barium sulfate
activities.summary: Mix sodium sulfate with excess barium chloride, filter off the white barium sulfate, wash it, dry it and weigh it, and work out the percentage yield (in duplicate).
terms: Preparing an insoluble salt: barium sulfate

activities.title: Sulfate by gravimetry
activities.summary: Precipitate the sulfate in a pipetted volume of an unknown solution as barium sulfate, filter, wash, dry and weigh it, and calculate the sulfate concentration (in duplicate).

activities.title: Chloride by gravimetry
activities.summary: Precipitate the chloride in a pipetted volume of an unknown solution as silver chloride with excess silver nitrate, filter, wash, dry and weigh it, and calculate the chloride concentration (in duplicate).

activities.title: Calcium carbonate in limestone by back titration
activities.summary: Dissolve powdered limestone in a measured excess of hydrochloric acid, titrate the acid left over with sodium hydroxide, and work out the percentage of calcium carbonate.
terms: Reacting a sample with a measured excess
Calcium carbonate in limestone by back titration

activities.title: How much acid does an antacid neutralise?
activities.summary: Dissolve a powdered antacid tablet in a measured excess of hydrochloric acid, titrate the acid left over, and work out how much stomach acid a gram of tablet neutralises.
terms: Reacting a sample with a measured excess
How much acid does an antacid neutralise?

activities.title: Flame tests for metal ions
activities.summary: Find the flame colours of lithium, sodium, potassium, calcium, strontium, barium and copper, see how a trace of sodium hides potassium and how cobalt-blue glass shows it, then identify the metal in an unknown.
terms: Atoms emit light of their own wavelengths

activities.title: Emission spectra with a hand spectroscope
activities.summary: Look at the flames of metal salts through a hand spectroscope: each element gives bright lines at its own wavelengths (sodium's at 589 nm, lithium's at 671 nm) and some molecules bands. Identify an unknown from its lines.
terms: Atoms emit light of their own wavelengths
Emission spectra with a hand spectroscope

activities.title: Finding a copper(II) concentration with the Beer–Lambert law
activities.summary: Make copper(II) sulfate standards from a stock, read their absorbance at 800 nm against a water blank, fit absorbance against concentration through the origin, and use the line to find the concentration of an unknown.
terms: Finding a copper(II) concentration with the Beer–Lambert law

activities.title: The pH of salt solutions
activities.summary: Measure the pH of six salt solutions with a calibrated pH meter and universal indicator, and explain why some salts give acidic or alkaline solutions though no acid or alkali was added.
terms: pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is
Acids give and bases take hydrogen ions

activities.title: Indicators and the pH scale
activities.summary: Test hydrochloric and ethanoic acids, water, sodium hydrogencarbonate, ammonia and sodium hydroxide with litmus, methyl orange, phenolphthalein, bromothymol blue and universal indicator, and compare the colours with pH-meter readings.
terms: pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is
Acids give and bases take hydrogen ions

activities.title: Identify an unknown salt
activities.summary: Identify the cation and the anion of an unknown salt by a flame test, sodium hydroxide and ammonia, an acid and limewater, silver nitrate and barium chloride. A different salt is drawn each run.
terms: Metal ions are identified by flame colour and hydroxide precipitates
Carbonate, halide and sulfate ions each have a test, done in acid

activities.title: The disappearing cross: concentration and rate
activities.summary: Add hydrochloric acid to sodium thiosulfate diluted to five concentrations and time how long the sulfur it forms takes to hide a cross drawn under the flask.
terms: More concentrated or hotter reactants collide more often and more energetically
The disappearing cross: concentration and rate

activities.title: The disappearing cross: temperature and rate
activities.summary: Warm diluted sodium thiosulfate to four temperatures, add acid and time how long the cross takes to disappear.
terms: More concentrated or hotter reactants collide more often and more energetically
The disappearing cross: temperature and rate

activities.title: The iodine clock: the order with respect to iodide
activities.summary: Time how long a persulfate–iodide mixture takes to turn starch blue-black with five iodide concentrations, and find the order of reaction with respect to iodide.
terms: A clock reaction times how long a fixed amount of product takes to form
The iodine clock: the order with respect to iodide

activities.title: The iodine clock: activation energy
activities.summary: Time the iodine clock at four temperatures and find the activation energy from an Arrhenius plot of ln(1/t) against 1/T.
terms: A clock reaction times how long a fixed amount of product takes to form

activities.title: Chromate and dichromate: an equilibrium you can see
activities.summary: Turn yellow chromate orange with acid and back with alkali, and pull the equilibrium towards chromate by precipitating barium chromate from orange dichromate.
terms: A system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in conditions
Chromate and dichromate: an equilibrium you can see

activities.title: Available chlorine in bleach by iodometric titration
activities.summary: Let diluted bleach liberate iodine from acidified potassium iodide, titrate the iodine with standard sodium thiosulfate to a starch end point, and work out the bleach’s available chlorine.
terms: An oxidising agent is measured by the iodine it releases from iodide
Available chlorine in bleach by iodometric titration

activities.title: Testing for a carboxylic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate
activities.summary: Add sodium hydrogencarbonate solution to ethanoic acid, ethanol and water, bubble any gas through limewater, and tell the carboxylic acid from the alcohol.
terms: Carboxylic acids are weak acids but strong enough to release CO₂ from carbonates
Testing for a carboxylic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate

activities.title: Testing for a C=C double bond with bromine water
activities.summary: Shake cyclohexene and cyclohexane with bromine water: the alkene decolourises it, the alkane does not.
terms: A functional group reacts the same way whatever molecule it is in
Testing for a C=C double bond with bromine water

activities.title: Primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols with acidified dichromate
activities.summary: Warm ethanol, propan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol with acidified potassium dichromate: the primary and secondary alcohols turn it from orange to green, the tertiary does not.
terms: A functional group reacts the same way whatever molecule it is in
Primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols with acidified dichromate

activities.title: Aldehydes and ketones: Tollens’ and Fehling’s tests
activities.summary: Warm ethanal and propanone with Tollens’ reagent and with Fehling’s solution: the aldehyde gives a silver mirror and a red precipitate, the ketone neither.
terms: A functional group reacts the same way whatever molecule it is in
Aldehydes and ketones: Tollens’ and Fehling’s tests

activities.title: The iodoform test for CH₃CO– and CH₃CH(OH)–
activities.summary: Warm ethanol, propan-2-ol, propanone and methanol with iodine and sodium hydroxide: those with a methyl group next to a C=O (or next to a CH(OH) that is oxidised to one) give pale yellow iodoform.
terms: A functional group reacts the same way whatever molecule it is in
The iodoform test for CH₃CO– and CH₃CH(OH)–

activities.title: Phenols with iron(III) chloride
activities.summary: Add neutral iron(III) chloride solution to phenol and to ethanol: the phenol turns violet, the alcohol does not.
terms: A functional group reacts the same way whatever molecule it is in

activities.title: Specific heat capacity of metals by the method of mixtures
activities.summary: Heat blocks of aluminium, copper and steel in hot water, drop each into cold water in an insulated cup, and work out each metal’s specific heat capacity from the rise in temperature.
terms: Specific heat capacity is the energy to warm 1 g of a material by 1 K
Specific heat capacity of metals by the method of mixtures

activities.title: The specific latent heat of fusion of ice
activities.summary: Melt a weighed mass of ice in warm water in an insulated cup, and work out from the fall in temperature how much energy each gram of ice takes to melt.
terms: Melting takes energy without a change of temperature
The specific latent heat of fusion of ice
specific latent heat of fusion of ice

activities.title: The pKa of acetic acid from a pH titration curve
activities.summary: Calibrate a pH meter with two buffers, titrate 25 mL of acetic acid with standardised sodium hydroxide in 1 mL portions, reading the pH after each, and find the pKa as the pH at half the equivalence volume.
terms: The pKa of acetic acid from a pH titration curve

activities.title: Cooling curve of stearic acid
activities.summary: Melt stearic acid in a hot water bath, let it cool in air, reading its temperature every 30 seconds, and find its freezing point from the flat part of the cooling curve.
terms: A pure substance freezes at a steady temperature, giving out latent heat

activities.title: Electrochemical cells: the Daniell cell
activities.summary: Build a zinc half-cell and a copper half-cell, join them with a salt bridge, and measure the cell potential; find which electrode is negative.

activities.title: Electrochemical cells: metals against copper
activities.summary: Measure the potential of magnesium, zinc, iron and lead half-cells against a copper half-cell and use them to place the metals in order of reactivity.

activities.title: Electrochemical cells: concentration cells
activities.summary: Join copper half-cells of 0.001 to 1 M copper(II) sulfate to a 1 M copper half-cell and relate the small cell potential to the ratio of concentrations.

activities.title: Electrochemical cells: the effect of concentration on a Daniell cell
activities.summary: Measure a zinc–copper cell with the copper(II) sulfate at 1, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 M and relate the change to the Nernst equation.
terms: Electrochemical cells: the effect of concentration on a Daniell cell

activities.title: Simple cells: two metals in an electrolyte
activities.summary: Stand pairs of metals in dilute acid, lemon juice and salt water and measure the voltage each pair gives; relate it to how far apart the metals are in the reactivity series.
terms: Simple cells: two metals in an electrolyte

activities.title: Conductivity of strong and weak electrolytes
activities.summary: Measure the conductivity of 0.1 M solutions of acids, alkalis, a salt and sugar and of deionised water, and sort them into strong, weak and non-electrolytes.
terms: Conductivity of strong and weak electrolytes

activities.title: Molar conductivity on dilution: strong and weak electrolytes
activities.summary: Measure the conductivity of potassium chloride and ethanoic acid at 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 M and compare how their molar conductivity changes on dilution.
terms: Molar conductivity on dilution: strong and weak electrolytes

activities.title: Water quality: pH, conductivity and dissolved solids
activities.summary: Measure the pH, conductivity and total dissolved solids of deionised water, rainwater, stream, tap, pond and diluted sea water, and compare them.
terms: Conductivity measures the dissolved ions, and so estimates the dissolved solids
Water quality: pH, conductivity and dissolved solids

activities.title: Electrolysis of aqueous solutions: the products
activities.summary: Electrolyse seven solutions between graphite electrodes, collect any gas at each electrode and test it, and work out the rules for which products form.
terms: Electrolysis of aqueous solutions: the products
Low-voltage DC power supply with ammeter

activities.title: Electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate: graphite against copper electrodes
activities.summary: Electrolyse copper(II) sulfate between graphite rods and between copper strips, and compare what happens at the anode.
terms: Electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate: graphite against copper electrodes
Low-voltage DC power supply with ammeter

activities.title: Electroplating copper and the Faraday constant
activities.summary: Plate copper from copper(II) sulfate between copper electrodes at three currents, weigh the electrodes before and after, and calculate the Faraday constant from the charge passed and the mass deposited.
terms: Electroplating copper and the Faraday constant
Low-voltage DC power supply with ammeter

activities.title: What makes iron rust?
activities.summary: Leave clean iron nails for three days in tap water, in boiled water under oil, in dry air over calcium chloride, and in salt water, and compare how much each rusts.

activities.title: Sacrificial protection: stopping iron rusting with another metal
activities.summary: Leave iron nails in salt water for three days alone and wrapped in zinc, magnesium and copper, and compare how much each nail rusts.
terms: Sacrificial protection: stopping iron rusting with another metal

activities.title: Boyle’s law: pressure and volume of a gas
activities.summary: Trap 50 mL of air in a sealed syringe connected to a pressure sensor, hold the plunger at volumes from 100 mL to 25 mL, and show that pressure × volume stays constant.
terms: Boyle’s law: pressure and volume of a gas

activities.title: Charles’s law: volume and temperature of a gas
activities.summary: Warm 40 mL of trapped air in a sealed syringe from 0 to 80 °C in water baths, read its volume at each temperature, and extrapolate to absolute zero.
terms: Charles’s law: volume and temperature of a gas

activities.title: The rate of ester hydrolysis at two temperatures
activities.summary: Mix equal amounts of sodium hydroxide and ethyl ethanoate at 25 °C and at 35 °C, follow the falling pH for 30 minutes, convert pH to hydroxide concentration, find the second-order rate constant from a plot of 1/[OH⁻] against time, and the activation energy from the two rate constants.
terms: Second-order kinetics and the integrated rate law
The rate of ester hydrolysis at two temperatures

activities.title: The relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid
activities.summary: Inject a small, known mass of a volatile liquid into a gas syringe in an oven at 100 °C, measure the volume of vapour, and calculate its relative molecular mass from pV = nRT.
terms: The relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid
relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid

activities.title: The vapour pressure of water and its enthalpy of vaporisation
activities.summary: Trap air over a little water in a sealed syringe, find the amount of air at 0 °C, then measure the volume from 30 to 90 °C; the extra volume beyond Charles’s law is water vapour, giving the vapour pressure at each temperature and, from a Clausius–Clapeyron plot, the enthalpy of vaporisation.
terms: The vapour pressure of water and its enthalpy of vaporisation

activities.title: The size of a molecule and the Avogadro constant from an oil film
activities.summary: Drop a dilute solution of oleic acid in ethanol onto water dusted with powder, measure the circular film it spreads into, and estimate the length of an oleic acid molecule and the Avogadro constant.
terms: The size of a molecule and the Avogadro constant from an oil film

activities.title: A heating curve: melting stearic acid
activities.summary: Warm solid stearic acid in a boiling tube in a water bath at 75 °C, reading its temperature every 30 seconds, and find its melting point from the level part of the heating curve.
terms: A heating curve: melting stearic acid

activities.title: Freezing-point depression: cooling curves of solutions
activities.summary: Cool tubes of water, sodium chloride and sucrose solutions in an ice2013salt freezing mixture, follow their temperatures, and compare their freezing points: the depression depends on the number of dissolved particles.
terms: Freezing-point depression: cooling curves of solutions

activities.title: Le Chatelier’s principle: the cobalt(II) chloride equilibrium
activities.summary: Shift the equilibrium between pink hexaaquacobalt(II) and blue tetrachlorocobaltate(II) by adding chloride, adding water, heating and cooling, and use the colour changes to find the sign of ΔH.
terms: Le Chatelier’s principle: the cobalt(II) chloride equilibrium

activities.title: Buffer pH and buffer capacity
activities.summary: Make an acetate buffer from equal volumes of 0.1 M acetic acid and 0.1 M sodium acetate, the same buffer diluted ten-fold, and a beaker of water. Add 0.1 M sodium hydroxide to each in 1 mL portions, reading the pH after each, and compare how well each resists the change.

activities.title: What is in a painkiller? Thin-layer chromatography
activities.summary: Spot aspirin, paracetamol and caffeine standards and an extract of an unknown tablet on a silica TLC plate, develop it in ethyl acetate, look at it under short-wave UV, work out each spot's Rf and decide which of the three the tablet contains.
terms: What is in a painkiller? Thin-layer chromatography

activities.title: Enthalpy of neutralisation by calorimetry
activities.summary: In a polystyrene-cup calorimeter, record the temperature of 50 mL of 1.0 M hydrochloric acid for three minutes, add 50 mL of 1.0 M sodium hydroxide and keep recording. Extrapolate the cooling line back to the moment of mixing to find the temperature rise, and work out the enthalpy of neutralisation. Repeat with ammonia.

activities.title: Simple and fractional distillation of an ethanol–water mixture
activities.summary: Distil 100 mL of 20 % (v/v) ethanol twice, once simply and once through a Vigreux column, collecting three 12 mL fractions each and noting the still-head temperature. Find each fraction's ethanol content from the mass of 10.00 mL, and compare the two methods.
terms: Simple and fractional distillation of an ethanol–water mixture
fractional distillation of an ethanol–water mixture

activities.title: Gram staining two bacteria
activities.summary: Make a smear of each of two broth cultures, heat-fix and Gram stain them, look at them under oil immersion, and classify each organism.

activities.title: Algae in a river: concentrating and counting cells
activities.summary: Spin down the algae in 12 mL of water from above, at and below a sewage outfall, take each pellet up in 0.5 mL, count four 1 mm² squares of a haemocytometer twice for each, and work back to cells per mL of river water.
terms: Concentrating a sample and correcting for it
Algae in a river: concentrating and counting cells

activities.title: Is it safe to swim? Viable counts and faecal indicator bacteria
activities.summary: Serially dilute water from two sites, spread nutrient agar for a total viable count and EMB agar for E. coli (green sheen) and other coliforms (pink); count plates of 30–300 colonies, and judge the water against a bathing guideline, knowing what a plate cannot show.
terms: Is it safe to swim? Viable counts and faecal indicator bacteria

activities.title: Is it what the label says? Checking two bioremediation cultures
activities.summary: Two products are sold as Pseudomonas putida for cleaning up oil-contaminated soil. Gram stain them, grow them on Pseudomonas selective agar, test oxidase, offer them hexadecane as the only carbon source, and run a P. putida-specific PCR on boiled colonies; then decide what each really is.
terms: Is it what the label says? Checking two bioremediation cultures

activities.title: Fuel in the soil: counting a degrader by spot plating
activities.summary: Four sterile-soil microcosms seeded with an alkane-degrading pseudomonad (with or without an alkane fuel, kept cold or on the bench for a day): suspend half a gram of each, dilute to 10⁻⁶, spot three 10 µL drops of every dilution on one plate, and count the spots two days later to see where the degrader multiplied.
terms: Temperature and substrate as limits to growth
Fuel in the soil: counting a degrader by spot plating

activities.title: What limits the clean-up? Designing a soil microcosm study
activities.summary: Seven soil microcosms seeded with an alkane degrader have spent a day under different conditions: fuel or none, fertiliser, drier or wetter, cooler or warmer. With six plates and six universals, choose a question, compare the right microcosms with replicate subsamples, spot plate and count them, and test the difference statistically.
terms: Changing one variable at a time
Limiting factors for growth (Liebig's law of the minimum)
Comparing two groups with a t-test
What limits the clean-up? Designing a soil microcosm study

activities.title: Trimethoprim for a urinary infection? MICs of two folate-pathway antibiotics
activities.summary: Two-fold dilutions of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole along a 96-well plate against a reference E. coli, a urinary isolate and S. aureus, with a solvent-only row; read the turbidity after a night at 37 °C, find each MIC and decide whether trimethoprim could treat the patient.
terms: The folate pathway as a drug target
Trimethoprim for a urinary infection? MICs of two folate-pathway antibiotics

activities.title: Better together? Checkerboards for two antibiotic pairs
activities.summary: Two broth checkerboards against E. coli: trimethoprim across sulfamethoxazole, and gentamicin across streptomycin. Read the turbidity after a night at 37 °C, find each drug's MIC alone and the fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) of each pair, and decide which pair is synergistic.
terms: Better together? Checkerboards for two antibiotic pairs

activities.title: Which mutations does it cause? A bacterial reversion test with two tester strains
activities.summary: Pour two histidine-requiring Salmonella tester strains in minimal top agar, test two coded compounds on discs against each, and a five-fold dose series of one of them; from the revertant colonies decide what kind of mutation each compound causes and why the dose response turns over.
terms: Mutagenicity against toxicity in a dose response

activities.title: Is it Lactobacillus acidophilus? A probiotic by Gram stain, MRS agar and PCR
activities.summary: Gram stain a reference Lactobacillus acidophilus beside Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli; grow the controls, a probiotic capsule and a fermented milk drink on MRS agar, which is selective for lactobacilli; and test colonies by a PCR specific for L. acidophilus (129 bp).
terms: Is it Lactobacillus acidophilus? A probiotic by Gram stain, MRS agar and PCR

activities.title: Isolating a pure culture from a mixture by streaking
activities.summary: Streak a mixed broth culture for single colonies, pick a golden colony into fresh broth, grow it overnight, and confirm by Gram stain that it is a pure Gram-positive coccus.
terms: A colony grows from a single cell
Isolating a pure culture from a mixture by streaking

activities.title: Counting live and dead yeast cells
activities.summary: Dilute a yeast culture ten-fold, stain it with trypan blue, count four squares of a haemocytometer, and report cells per mL and viability.
terms: Counting live and dead yeast cells

activities.title: A bacterial growth curve and the doubling time
activities.summary: Grow E. coli in LB broth at 37 °C, take a sample every 30 minutes for five hours, read its turbidity at 600 nm against broth, and find the doubling time from the exponential phase.
terms: A bacterial growth curve and the doubling time

activities.title: A viable count by serial dilution and spread plating
activities.summary: Make a ten-fold dilution series of an overnight E. coli culture, spread 100 µL of the 10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁶ and 10⁻⁷ dilutions on duplicate LB plates, incubate overnight, count the plates with 30 to 300 colonies and work out the viable count in CFU per mL.
terms: Colony-forming units and the countable range
A viable count by serial dilution and spread plating

activities.title: The minimum inhibitory concentration of ampicillin
activities.summary: Make two-fold dilutions of ampicillin from 128 to 0.25 µg/mL across a 96-well plate, inoculate one row with a susceptible E. coli and one with an unknown strain, incubate overnight, read the turbidity at 600 nm and find each strain's MIC.
terms: The minimum inhibitory concentration of ampicillin

activities.title: Identifying an unknown bacterium
activities.summary: Identify an unknown culture, one of five teaching organisms, from its Gram stain, a catalase test, an oxidase test and its growth and colour on MacConkey agar.
terms: Identification from a few discriminating tests

activities.title: Antibiotic susceptibility by disc diffusion
activities.summary: Seed Mueller–Hinton plates with standardised suspensions of E. coli, S. aureus and an unknown isolate, press on ampicillin, tetracycline, kanamycin and chloramphenicol discs, incubate overnight, measure the inhibition zones and classify the isolate.

activities.title: Microbes everywhere: where contamination comes from, and keeping it out
activities.summary: Leave plates open to the air for different times and press fingertips on agar before and after washing; pass loopfuls between sterile broths with flamed necks beside an unopened control; plate pond water at two temperatures; stab two cultures into agar deeps. Two days later, count, look and explain.
terms: Microbes everywhere: where contamination comes from, and keeping it out

activities.title: Transforming E. coli with a GFP plasmid
activities.summary: Heat-shock competent E. coli with the pGLO plasmid, plate transformed and untransformed cells on LB, LB/ampicillin and LB/ampicillin/arabinose, grow them overnight, count colonies, look for fluorescence and calculate the transformation efficiency.
terms: Selection by an antibiotic resistance marker
Transforming E. coli with a GFP plasmid

activities.title: Is it an operon? RT-PCR across gene junctions
activities.summary: PCR on cDNA from E. coli grown with and without IPTG, with primers inside lacZ, lacY and lacA and across the junctions between them, a housekeeping gene (gapA), a no-RT control and genomic DNA, to show that lac is one inducible polycistronic mRNA.
terms: Is it an operon? RT-PCR across gene junctions

activities.title: End-binding or coating? An agarose gel shift with two DNA lengths
activities.summary: Titrate a Gam-like DNA-end-binding protein onto a supercoiled plasmid and onto 300 bp and 900 bp linear DNAs, run the reactions on an agarose gel, and from the shifts decide whether it needs DNA ends, whether it coats the DNA, and roughly how tightly it binds.
terms: Binding-site size from the saturated shift
End-binding or coating? An agarose gel shift with two DNA lengths

activities.title: What changed? Finding mutations and reversions by sequencing
activities.summary: Sequence PCR products from two histidine-requiring Salmonella mutants and three of their revertants, find the mutated gene by searching reference sequences, read each mutation and each reversion from alignments, and spot a read from a mixed colony.
terms: Missense, nonsense, silent and frameshift mutations
Identity and coverage in a sequence search
What changed? Finding mutations and reversions by sequencing

activities.title: A binding isotherm by EMSA: fitting the shift for an apparent Kd
activities.summary: Titrate a DNA-binding protein onto a 900 bp linear DNA at eight concentrations, run the reactions on an agarose gel, measure how far each band has shifted relative to the free DNA, fit a Langmuir isotherm for the maximal shift and an apparent Kd, and judge the fit by its residuals.
terms: A binding isotherm by EMSA: fitting the shift for an apparent Kd

activities.title: Where does replication start? Origins, forks and the cell cycle from data
activities.summary: Work out two microbes' genome structure, origins, fork speed, inter-origin distance and S phase from pulsed-field gels, ARS assays, replication profiles, DNA combing and flow cytometry, and decide which Earth organisms each resembles.
terms: Where does replication start? Origins, forks and the cell cycle from data

activities.title: A prophage gene from data: homology search and RNA-seq
activities.summary: Decide from a BLASTp hit table and a prophage search whether a bacterium carries a Mu-like prophage with a Gam homologue, then from RNA-seq counts (rich against starvation medium, triplicates) whether that gene is transcribed and whether it belongs to the competence response.
terms: A prophage gene from data: homology search and RNA-seq

activities.title: Amplifying the GFP gene by PCR and sizing it on a gel
activities.summary: Set up a PCR for the GFP gene of pGLO and a no-template control, run 30 cycles, run both beside a 1 kb ladder on a 1 % agarose gel, and estimate the product's size from the ladder.
terms: Amplifying the GFP gene by PCR and sizing it on a gel

activities.title: Mapping a plasmid with restriction enzymes
activities.summary: Digest pBR322 with EcoRI alone and with EcoRI, BamHI and PstI in pairs, run the digests and the uncut plasmid beside a 1 kb ladder, size the fragments and work out where the BamHI and PstI sites lie relative to the EcoRI site.
terms: Restriction enzymes cut at specific sites
Deducing a map from single and double digests
Supercoiled, nicked and linear DNA run differently
Mapping a plasmid with restriction enzymes

activities.title: Genotyping a taste-receptor SNP by PCR-RFLP
activities.summary: Amplify a 221 bp stretch of the bitter-taste receptor gene TAS2R38 from three people's DNA, digest the products with HaeIII, which cuts only the taster allele, run them on a 3 % agarose gel and work out each person's genotype from the band pattern.
terms: A SNP that creates or destroys a restriction site
Genotyping a taste-receptor SNP by PCR-RFLP

activities.title: Lac repressor binding its operator: a gel-shift assay
activities.summary: Mix a fluorescent lac operator probe with LacI from 0 to 10 nM, run the mixtures on a native gel, image the probe, measure the share of it shifted into the slower LacI–DNA complex in each lane, and fit the binding curve to find the dissociation constant. Two more lanes test IPTG and an excess of unlabelled operator.
terms: Lac repressor binding its operator: a gel-shift assay

activities.title: Real-time PCR: a standard curve, efficiency and copy number
activities.summary: Make ten-fold dilutions of a pGLO plasmid standard (10⁷ copies/µL), run them in triplicate with an unknown and no-template controls in a SYBR Green qPCR for the GFP gene, and finish with a melt curve. Plot Cq against log₁₀ copies, find the efficiency from the slope, and read the unknown's copy number.
terms: Real-time PCR and the quantification cycle
Real-time PCR: a standard curve, efficiency and copy number

activities.title: Checking clones by restriction digestion: insert and orientation
activities.summary: A 6.0 kb fragment was cloned into the BamHI site of a 3.0 kb vector. Digest the empty vector and two clones with BamHI and with EcoRI, run the six digests beside a 1 kb ladder, and decide whether each clone carries the insert and in which orientation.
terms: Checking clones by restriction digestion: insert and orientation

activities.title: Which bacteria carry a resistance gene? Colony PCR, a gel and an ampicillin test
activities.summary: Suspend four E. coli isolates from treated effluent and two control strains in water; test each suspension by colony PCR for the beta-lactamase gene blaTEM (516 bp) on a gel, and by growth in ampicillin broth; then compare genotype with phenotype.
terms: Which bacteria carry a resistance gene? Colony PCR, a gel and an ampicillin test

activities.title: Fluoroquinolone resistance by PCR-RFLP: gyrA codon 83
activities.summary: Amplify the quinolone resistance-determining region of gyrA from four urinary E. coli isolates and a sensitive reference strain, digest the products with HinfI, whose site at codon 83 the Ser83Leu mutation removes, and read each isolate's genotype from a 2 % gel.
terms: A point mutation that destroys a restriction site
Fluoroquinolone resistance by PCR-RFLP: gyrA codon 83
